name: Coldseam The Disgraced Judge's Last Formal Set
description:
Once a Spire governance robe, now stripped of insignia and carefully reworked into something that reads as formal without declaring allegiance. Deep charcoal wool-analog longcoat — the judicial gold trim has been unpicked, leaving ghost-lines in the weave. Beneath: a pressed high-collar shirt in off-white, slightly yellowed at the cuffs from repeated laundering. Slim formal trousers, hand-pressed. Worn black oxfords, resoled twice. A single neural port at the temple is left uncovered — the port housing is engraved with a case number that no longer exists in any public record.

Coldseam makes nothing this formal; this is a one-off commission from a tailor who asked no questions.
functionality: Formal presentation without active affiliation signaling, neural port left accessible, resoled boots for extended wear, hand-pressed construction requiring no powered maintenance.
what_it_says: Someone who once held enormous power and lost it — still carrying the posture, no longer carrying the title.
worn_by: defrocked governance officials navigating lower tiers
characters defined by a specific downfall
story_hooks: The case number engraved on the neural port housing was expunged — finding out why requires accessing a court archive that officially burned in 2189.
Someone in the Spire is paying a Shelf fixer to locate this person before they talk to a journalist.
The ghost-lines where the judicial trim was removed are visible under certain lighting — in the right circles, people still recognize what this coat used to be.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately austere formal silhouette with intentional erasure. Deep charcoal longcoat drapes with judicial precision, but the absence of gold trim creates an unsettling void—ghost-lines visible in certain light where insignia once lived. The overall effect is 'authority stripped bare,' commanding yet haunted. High-collared off-white shirt reads corporate-formal but carries the patina of obsessive care. Paired with slim charcoal trousers and worn black oxfords, it presents as someone still performing formality long after losing the right to.
physical_description.fit: Tailored slim through the torso and legs; the longcoat is cut precisely but hangs with a faint asymmetry suggesting it was altered from original specifications. High collar sits rigid. Overall posture when worn suggests someone accustomed to standing for long periods under scrutiny.
physical_description.primary_material: Charcoal synth-wool blend (judicial-grade, high durability); off-white synthetic cotton-analog for shirt; black ballistic leather oxfords showing legitimate wear and resoled repairs
physical_description.texture: The coat weave is smooth but slightly raised where gold thread was removed—visible as fine scoring under oblique light. Shirt fabric is pressed to near-brittleness at the collar and cuffs. Leather oxfords are burnished dark, with visible creasing at the toe and heel from repeated wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal (primary), off-white/cream (secondary), black (accents). The ghosted gold lines in the coat weave create a subtle metallic undertone only visible in certain lighting—a scar in the fabric.
physical_description.closures: Concealed magnetic snaps on the longcoat (replacing original lacing points); traditional buttons on the shirt (replacement buttons, slightly mismatched); leather laces on oxfords (re-tied multiple times, knots worn smooth)
distinctive_features: Ghost-lines in the weave where judicial gold trim was unpicked
Visible repair seams where the coat was altered to remove insignia panels
Neural port at the temple (engraved with a case number no longer in any public record)
Cuffs of the shirt yellowed from repeated laundering—evidence of obsessive care
Oxfords resoled twice (visible stitching on the sole edges)
High collar sits at an almost uncomfortable angle—custom-fitted
Hand-press creases in trousers maintained with ritualistic precision
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1/2 origins (judicial formal wear), deliberately downgraded to Tier 3 (working-class salvage). The quality of materials and tailoring remain high-tier, but the presentation and condition signal deliberate descent.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this announces: 'I was someone with institutional power and chose to walk away.' It reads as either penitent, defiant, or broken—context-dependent. The uncovered neural port suggests either confidence or recklessness. Marks the wearer as Spire-adjacent but no longer aligned; likely triggers recognition from corporate security systems.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine in structure (obsessively maintained), but visibly aged and bearing evidence of alteration. The garment itself is well-kept but weathered by meaning—every maintenance ritual and wear pattern tells a story of deliberate downgrade.
